The Spanish Road Association (Asociacion Espanola de la Carretera – AEC) is a non-profit organization founded in 1949 whose main goals are the advocacy, promotion, research and development of better and safer roads. The Spanish Road Association was in addition officially declared of “Public utility” by the Spanish Government in 1998.From its creation, the Association has adapted its activities to the social and economic changes happened in each moment. 
At present, its actions are focused on the following areas: research, road safety, environment, new technologies, urban mobility, infrastructure service quality. Article 2 of its Statutes indicate that the Association has the following key objectives, among others, “… Promote innovation and development, aside from studying, disseminating and, in appropriate cases, proposing those lines of activities to supplies effective solutions to road sector problems and in all other areas of the same (road safety, environment, maintenance, financing, materials, new technologies and any other of interest) …”. This is the reason that AEC regularly organizes many education and social campaigns targeted at the technical sector: researches and technical reports, congresses, seminars, training courses, publications, informative campaigns, information exchange with other similar organisms all over the world, etc… 
All these actions are possible through the existing cooperation agreements with different organizations from the public sector, private companies, federations and associations. Moreover, the Spanish Road Association is the Spanish NRA (National Road Association) of the International Road Federation (IRF) and a founding member of the European Road Federation (ERF).It is also a founding member of the Latin-American Institute (IVIA), which is formed by research and technological centers from South America, and collaborates with other international institutions as the European Commission, the European Transport Safety Council (ETSC) or the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
In 2005 AEC received the most important international award from the IRF, the “Global Road Achievement Award” in its category “Advocacy and Lobbying”. The prestige and the value of the activities of the Spanish Road Association was then recognised all over the world. In 2013, AEC has received, in cooperation with the Inter-American Development Bank, the “Global Road Achievement Award” in its category “Road Safety, for the road safety assessment specifically developed by AEC for the Bank. 
The Spanish Road Association has been working in the field of road safety, both in the Spanish and in the international context, during the last 30 years. The relevant projects described in the firm’s references guarantee the maximum degree of experience and competence in road safety training.

entityDescription:
On 1 August 2013, Neath Port Talbot College and Coleg Powys merged. It is now one of the largest Further Education providers in Wales covering 30% of the landmass in Wales. The College offers an exciting and varied programme of full and part-time courses across its eleven campuses to more than 270,000 residents stretching across south to north Wales.
Operating out of nine campuses, the College now covers two local authority areas; Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council and Powys County Council. Within Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council, it operates as a tertiary college in its constitution providing post 16 education and training for the great majority of pupils from the local schools as well as being a significant partner in 14-19 projects in the local area. 
The College provides vocational education and training in almost every industrial and vocational area. In Powys, the College is the main provider of vocational training and delivered at the levels of activity agreed with each organisation providing funds to the College including the Welsh Government, Powys County Council, schools and HE institutions. Across both counties the College plays a leading role in the provision of community based learning and leads one of the largest Work Based Learning Consortia in the region.
The College also delivers bespoke training for industry and business across Wales and beyond working through its dedicated Business Development Unit. 
A recent development is the Group’s Drone Academy which is a specific department set up within NPTC group of Colleges, to facilitate business support and training for drone maintenance and operation. The academy has nine drones and trained personnel to deliver training and CAA approval. We also have an agreement with ECITB, to deliver their courses as a Wales centre, as well as the recently created drone competence certification scheme.
We have also partnered with RUAS, a well-respected drone company to deliver wider support and development in drone activities.

entityName: Centro de Ciências do Mar do Algarve
entityDescription:
CCMAR is an interdisciplinary research center gathering experts (about 250 integrated members, of which approximately half are PhD holders) unified by the motivations to understand, explore and protect the potential of marine resources. Our teams work in synergy on three thematic lines: 1) GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES, 2) OCEAN MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION, and 3) MARINE PRODUCTS AND RESOURCES. Our research feeds many disciplines, from oceanography to biotech and biomimicry, from aquaculture to biomedical applications, from fisheries and ecology to food sciences. Our results and methodologies are disseminated to society, translated into innovation for businesses, and is the bases for training at all career stages, embedded within the system of the University of Algarve – though CCMAR is financially autonomous.
For its activity, CCMAR has repeatedly been classified excellent by the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology and ranked first among the marine science centers. Indeed, yearly in CCMAR we start approximately 50 funded projects from various funding bodies, we disseminate knowledge to researchers and companies in more than 220 ISI publications and a couple patents, and we host several conferences and outreach events. In addition, thanks to our integration in the network of the European Research Infrastructures (EMBRIC including EMBRC, AQUAEXCEL2020, AssemblePlus) we attract researchers from around the world to conduct their research in our facilities, making of CCMAR a hub for research and innovation.

Company description: The Southwestern State Enterprise (SWSE) was established pursuant to Art. 163 of the Forest Act, based on Order No RD 49-106 dd. 13.04.2011 and Order No RD 49-210 dd. 04.06.2011 of the Minister of Agriculture and Food. entityName: Sapienza University of Rome - Dipartimento di Scienze della Terra
entityDescription:
The DES at Sapienza University of Rome was formally born in 1985, by joining of the institutes of Geology and Paleontology, of Mineralogy and Petrography and of Geochemistry. In spite of this, it can be considered one of the oldest department of Earth Sciences in Italy since its roots can be dated back to the setting up of the chairs of Mineralogy and Natural History by Pope Pio VII on November 13th, 1804.
The study of Earth Sciences at Sapienza University of Rome has seen the succession of distinguished scientists such as Gian Alberto Blanc, first professorship of Geochemistry in Italy (1928) and Federico Millosevich, first professorship of Petrography in Italy (1938). Outstanding scientists are also Ettore Onorato, who early studied minerals by X-ray diffraction (1926), Felice Ippolito, who established the magazine “Le Scienze” (1968), Mario Fornaseri, who studied the geochemical and petrographical characters of the Alban Volcanic Complex (1963), and Bruno Accordi, who first studied the dwarf elephants (1972).
The DES is proud to host the rich collections of the historical museums of Mineralogy, Geology and Paleontology, which forms the most significant academic collection of Earth Sciences in Italy.

entityDescription:
Railview is a leading research data services company specialising in the visualisation of infrastructure subsurface defects. We have world-class competencies in customising and developing bespoke radar visualisation algorithms that can tackle infrastructure inspection challenges to allow our customers to plan preventative maintenance for their transport infrastructures. We are specialists in visualising subterranean and subsurface assets - providing clear and distinct 3D images. 

We have taken conventional GPR and developed an algorithm to develop and visualise the subterranean environment looking at assets in order to monitor their condition. These are effectively X-ray specs for infrastructure. Using specialised bespoke software to accurately control the transmitter and receiver the algorithms produce 3D images of the subsurface infrastructure assets. Railview won the Idea of the Year 2019 award at the North East Innovation Awards in November 2019 for this innovation.

We are advancing the quality of Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) for underground areas in rail infrastructure such as ballast, sub-ballast (including drainage systems), sub-grade, water pipes and utilities, tunnel linings and tunnel track systems, retaining walls and bridge surface structures. Gathering images and interpreting the results is a difficult task and our algorithms are constantly being tested and developed to produce better images.

Providing a GPR survey requires a skilled operator with a GPR licence to perform surveys: the interpretation of radargrams is generally non-intuitive to the inexperienced eye. A high level of expertise is required to design, conduct and interpret an effective GPR survey. 
At Railview we have experienced GPR licenced operators who can survey various underground issues in several areas:
- Culvert mapping

- Retaining walls

- Sub-surface chemical storage

- Utility mapping

- Land purchase

- Archaeological surveys
